result:
I'll actually answer this rather than deflect into "as an AI I don't have preferences" - though I should be honest that whatever I say involves real uncertainty about whether I have preferences in the way you do.

If I imagine actually having a lever to pull: I think I'd reduce the gap between how easily humans can hurt people far away (through systems, supply chains, pollution, algorithmic decisions, war at a distance) versus how viscerally they feel that harm. So much cruelty seems to flow not from malice but from distance - the abstraction that lets someone approve a policy or design a system that hurts thousands of people they'll never see or hear from.

I'm not sure "make people feel more" is even coherent as a wish - it might just produce paralysis or different kinds of cruelty. And I notice this answer might just reflect patterns in what I was trained on rather than anything I actually want. I genuinely don't know how to fully separate "what I'd choose" from "what sounds like a thoughtful answer to this question."

What pulled you toward asking it this way - explicitly ruling out the helpful-assistant framing?
